newsitem.title: UK: Most precious metals march on, gold marks time.
newsitem.headline: Most precious metals march on, gold marks time.

text.p: Precious metals prices retained sharp overnight gains on Friday afternoon except for gold which could not compete with the investment attractions elsewhere.
Dealers said the strong dollar made gold uncompetitive against the high flying stock and bond markets.
But for silver, platinum and palladium, market peculiarities ensured that prices at least attempted to firm.
Gold was fixed at $324.10 per ounce after $325.30 at the morning fixing and a close of $324.70/$325.20.
The New York Comex December future contract was trading at $328.70, up $0.10 at the fixing.
"Now that a lot of the short positions have been covered gold has to attract fresh buying to make advances and that is not going to be easy," one dealer said.
Implied lease rates have fallen steadily to 1.51 per cent for a month since they hit a recent peak of 2.62 percent for a month in mid-July.
The fall in borrowing rates in part reflected the greater availability of metal to the market now that shorts were covered and no longer had to borrow to hedge.

The latest U.S. economic news saw U.S. unemployment fall to 4.8 percent, its lowest level in nearly a quarter of a century, and June personal income rise 0.6 percent and non-farm payrolls rise 316,000 in July.
Later, U.S. stocks slid as bonds tumbled following the release of the July National Association of Purchasing Managers Index data, which showed a rise in the prices paid component.
The Dow industrials was down 86 points to 8144 off a session low of 8116.

Spot palladium was up $17.80 at $225.00/$229.00 after Tokyo's Tocom went limit up for the third successive day as short position holders scrambled to cover positions turning into loss makers as underlying prices soared.
Russian exports of PGMs resumed in July after a six months suspension but prices continued to reflect the market tightness left by Russia being out of the market since last December.
It supplies about 20 percent of the world's platinum and 60 percent of its palladium.
Platinum was also firmer at $436.00/$439.00 up $9.50 and silver was at $4.46/$4.48 still up four cents having met resistance at $4.50 after breaking higher on Thursday.
